stakeholder: Oncology patients at MD Anderson receiving Watson recommendations
harm_description: Cancer patients receive treatment recommendations from AI that contradict current clinical evidence or physician judgment. Treatment delays or incorrect regimen choices occur when patients or physicians over-rely on AI suggestions without independent verification. Risk is highest for patients with rare cancer types where training data is sparse.
existing_controls: None in the Watson case - the system relied on vendor claims without independent clinical validation. MD Anderson physicians had ultimate authority but faced time pressure when overriding AI recommendations.
proposed_controls: Mandatory clinical validation: require independent physician panel to review all treatment recommendations against current clinical guidelines. Document training data composition including diversity of patient populations. Establish minimum evidence quality thresholds for recommendations. Create explicit uncertainty quantification for rare cancer types.
human_oversight: Subspecialist oncologists review all treatment recommendations with final treatment decision authority remaining with the treating physician. AI recommendations are advisory only with documented physician review required before patient discussion.
monitoring_metric: Treatment recommendation agreement rate between AI and independent physician panel; percentage of recommendations contradicted by current clinical evidence
trigger_threshold: Below 90% agreement rate on validation set; any recommendation contradicting established clinical guidelines without documented justification
response_action: Suspend specific cancer type recommendations pending re-validation. Trigger immediate case review for patients who received potentially incorrect recommendations.

stakeholder: Patients relying on Theranos test results for medication management
harm_description: Patients taking blood thinner medications received incorrect test results leading to potentially dangerous dosing decisions. Incorrect results could cause life-threatening bleeding (if INR falsely low) or blood clots (if INR falsely high). Patients and physicians made irreversible treatment decisions based on fraudulent data.
existing_controls: None in the Theranos case - the company lacked quality management systems, independent validation, and regulatory compliance. Test results were provided without adequate verification against reference standards.
proposed_controls: Mandatory external validation: require all diagnostic outputs to be verified against independent reference standards before patient delivery. Establish quality management system with statistical process control. Implement zero-tolerance policy for providing results outside validated operating range. Require FDA clearance before market deployment of diagnostic features.
human_oversight: Clinical laboratory supervisor reviews all quality control metrics daily. External proficiency testing program with blind samples submitted quarterly. Accreditation maintenance requirements with corrective action protocols.
monitoring_metric: Percentage of results within acceptable error range of reference standard; proficiency testing pass rate; QC coefficient of variation
trigger_threshold: Any result showing systematic bias above acceptable limits; proficiency testing failure; QC metric trending toward out-of-specification
response_action: Immediately halt result reporting for affected test types. Notify all patients who received potentially incorrect results within 24 hours. Establish hotline with physician consultation.

high_risk_moment: Triage urgency classification for emergency symptoms
stakeholder: Rural patients with limited healthcare access receiving AI triage recommendations
harm_description: Rural patients with serious conditions such as chest pain, difficulty breathing, or stroke symptoms receive inappropriately low urgency classification. Patients delay seeking emergency care based on AI reassurance. Time-critical treatment windows are missed resulting in preventable death or disability. This harm is especially severe because rural patients have no alternative access to verify AI recommendations.
existing_controls: Basic disclaimer text in user interface but research shows users frequently ignore disclaimers especially under stress. Emergency escalation prompts exist but may be dismissed as overcautious. Vietnamese language comprehension may be limited for medical terminology.
proposed_controls: Graduated escalation with mandatory acknowledgment: require users to explicitly confirm understanding of emergency symptoms before dismissing high-urgency recommendations. Add symptom checklist with red flag triggers before AI processing. Implement voice call capability for emergency symptoms connecting directly to emergency services. Design for low-literacy users with pictographic emergency indicators.
human_oversight: Physician on-call available for real-time escalation 24/7. Customer support trained to identify over-reliance patterns. Monthly audit of all low-urgency recommendations for patients with subsequently confirmed serious diagnoses.
monitoring_metric: Percentage of confirmed emergency cases that received appropriate (red/orange) triage classification; percentage of patients with serious diagnoses who initially received low-urgency recommendations; delayed-care incident rate
trigger_threshold: Below 97% appropriate emergency classification rate; any confirmed serious diagnosis (stroke MI sepsis) that received blue/green urgency; any delayed-care incident reported
response_action: Immediately escalate to physician callback for affected user. Trigger follow-up call within 2 hours. Convene incident review within 24 hours. Update model with affected symptom patterns.

stakeholder: Minority patients and low-income populations receiving algorithmic care recommendations
harm_description: Clinical decision support algorithms recommend different care pathways based on race or socioeconomic status in ways that reflect historical inequities rather than patient medical need. Black patients are less likely to be recommended for specialist care. Low-income patients are directed to lower-resource facilities. These recommendations perpetuate systemic healthcare disparities.
existing_controls: None or inadequate: most healthcare organizations lack systematic bias auditing of AI systems. Performance metrics are often not disaggregated by demographic groups.
proposed_controls: Comprehensive demographic parity testing: require all triage and care pathway recommendations to be tested for demographic bias before deployment and with every model update. Use multiple fairness metrics (demographic parity, equalized odds, calibration). Establish oversight committee including patient advocates from affected communities. Publish bias testing methodology in transparency reports.
human_oversight: Biweekly demographic parity review by Healthcare AI Ethics Board. External audit of bias metrics annually. Patient advocate liaison reviews all fairness-related escalations.
monitoring_metric: Statistical parity gap across race ethnicity age gender geographic region and socioeconomic status in: urgency classification rates; emergency escalation rates; appropriate care recommendation rates
trigger_threshold: Any statistically significant disparity (p<0.05) exceeding 5 percentage points in any metric for any demographic group
response_action: Pause affected recommendation workflows pending bias investigation. Convene emergency Healthcare AI Ethics Board meeting within 48 hours. Implement interim manual review for affected demographic groups.

stakeholder: Patients taking multiple medications receiving AI-generated medication information
harm_description: AI generates incorrect medication interaction information or provides hallucinated drug compatibility warnings. Patients discontinue necessary medications or make dosing errors based on false AI-generated information. Dangerous drug interactions are missed because the AI generates plausible-sounding but incorrect advice. Patients with complex medication regimens (elderly, chronic disease patients) are at highest risk.
existing_controls: Medication database licensing - but AI can generate hallucinations that appear to cite database information without actual retrieval verification.
proposed_controls: Pure retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with zero generative capability for medication content: all medication interactions and contraindications must come directly from validated database queries with no AI interpretation. Display source database citation for every medication-related output. Remove any capability for AI to generate novel medication content.
human_oversight: Pharmacist review of all medication-related system outputs before patient delivery during pilot phase. Mandatory database citation display for all medication queries. Zero-hallucination testing requirement: medication accuracy must achieve 100% on validation set.
monitoring_metric: Percentage of medication information queries returning database-verified content; hallucination rate in medication-related outputs; pharmacist error detection rate
trigger_threshold: Any hallucination detected in medication outputs; below 99.5% database verification rate on monthly audit
response_action: Pause medication interaction feature immediately on any hallucination detection. Notify all users who received potentially incorrect medication information within 24 hours. Implement mandatory pharmacist review until system is revalidated.
